title: Latency provenance notebook for microburst investigations
content:
Context
This is a lightweight, hands-on notebook for tracking and triaging short, high-amplitude latency spikes ("microbursts") that show up as very narrow but deep tail events in token-serving pipelines. Goal is to: 1) reliably detect microbursts, 2) identify provenance (which layer—routing, batching, kv-cache, model cold-start, GPU queueing, network), and 3) make compact dashboard + trace artifacts that an oncall operator can use in the first 10 minutes.

Why a separate doc?
- Many existing observability notes focus on broad SLOs and dashboards. Microbursts are transient and often hidden in aggregates; they need narrower signals, different sampling, and quicker drill-down anchors.
- This is intentionally tactical: pragmatic queries, span attributes, and a minimal dashboard wireframe.

High-level hypothesis list (what typically causes microbursts)
- Autoscaler/placement churn: nodes temporarily overloaded while replicas spin up/tear down.
- Batching pressure: sudden queueing leading to oversized batch formation which then exposes long per-token latency.
- KV cache coldness: unexpected cache misses for long sessions or tenant-specific key loss.
- Model variant fallback: routing to heavier model variant when primary is constrained.
- Tracing/sample bias: missing spans or low sampling hiding root causes.
- Network flapping between control plane and workers (rare but catastrophic).

Minimum telemetry signals to collect (definitions, recommended units and cardinalities)
- microburst_windowed_p50_ms, microburst_windowed_p95_ms, microburst_windowed_p99_ms: sliding-windowed token latency per 1s/5s window (ms). Cardinality: per-route, per-model, per-region, per-tenant (if multi-tenant).
- token_service_queue_depth: instantaneous queue length before batch formation (count). Useful at 100ms resolution.
- batch_sizes_histogram: histogram of formed batch sizes (buckets 1,2,4,8,16,32,64+). Emit with model and route tags.
- kv_cache_hit_rate_5m_by_tenant: percent over 5m window; include tag for cache_shard_id.
- gpu_scheduler_wait_ms: time waiting in GPU scheduler queue before kernel launch (ms).
- model_variant_fallbacks_count: counter of fallback events; label with from_variant, to_variant, reason.
- infra_scale_events: event marker emitted when autoscaler changes allocation (up/down) with reason tag.

Span & trace conventions to enable fast provenance mapping
- root span: request_handle (attributes: request_id, tenant_id, route, route_version, model, seq_len_hint)
- batch span: batch_form (attrs: batch_id, batch_size, batching_strategy, enqueue_ts, dequeue_ts)
- kv span: kv_lookup (attrs: cache_key, shard_id, hit_bool, ttl_ms)
- scheduler span: gpu_queue (attrs: node_id, gpu_id, queue_start_ts, queue_end_ts, estimated_wait_ms)
- kernel span: kernel_exec (attrs: model_variant, quant_level, forward_ms, tokens_produced)
- network span: controlplane_call (attrs: cp_endpoint, latency_ms, status_code)
- fallback span: model_route_fallback (attrs: requested_variant, chosen_variant, cause)
- annotator span: sampled_user_prompt_rewrite (attrs: rewrite_hash)

Sampling policy for microburst investigations (proposal)
- Default sampling: 1% traces across all traffic for general health.
- Adaptive target sampling: when microburst_windowed_p95_ms > threshold for a route, raise sampling to 100% for requests in that route for 30s window and capture full trace. Also attach example of problematic requests to a short-term trace store (48h retention).
- Severity-weighted capture: capture full traces for any request where kernel_exec.forward_ms > 5x baseline_p95 for model.

Dashboard wireframe (compact page for oncall)
Top row (alert + quick health):
- Microburst alert banner (boolean): rule triggers when route-level microburst_p95 spike and token_service_queue_depth > X. Banner includes last spike time and quick link to trace search.
- Route-level heatmap (time vs route): color = microburst_p95 normalized. Hover shows last offending tenant and sample request_id.
Second row (provenance slices):
- Stack waterfall chart: decomposed median wait times for last 5 spikes (queueing vs batching vs kv vs kernel). Each bar clickable to open trace.
- Batch-size distribution sparkline with anomaly shading for recent window.
Third row (investigation table):
- Recent microburst events: columns = start_ts, duration_s, top-tenant, batch_size_median, kv_miss_rate, fallback_occurred(T/F), trace_link. Rows clickable to open trace/replay.
Fourth row (cheap probes & knobs):
- Synthetic probe success rate for 100ms-1s probe test (per-region).
- Autoscaler event timeline (markers) overlaying the latency timeline.

Quick SQL/PromQL examples (replace metric names for hosting)
- Detect candidate microburst windows (PromQL-ish):
  max_over_time(microburst_windowed_p95_ms[30s]) > 300
- Find routes with >=5 spikes in last 24h:
  count_over_time((microburst_windowed_p95_ms > 200)[24h:1h]) by (route) > 5
- KV miss rate per tenant (5m):
  (sum(increase(kv_lookup_total{hit="false"}[5m])) by (tenant) / sum(increase(kv_lookup_total[5m])) by (tenant)) * 100
- Batch size median (5m): use histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(batch_sizes_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))

Investigation runbook (first 10 / next 60 / escalation)
- First 0-10 minutes (operator):
  1) Check alert banner context: route, start_ts, sample trace links.
  2) Open the per-route heatmap and confirm whether spike is isolated or multi-route. If isolated -> likely tenant or route config. If cross-route -> infra (autoscaling, GPU queueing).
  3) Check token_service_queue_depth and batch_sizes at spike time. If queue depth high and batch size distribution shifts up, suspect batching pressure.
  4) Query kv_cache_hit_rate_5m_by_tenant for top tenants in that window. If a tenant has miss spike, add to suspect list.
  5) Open 3 full traces (adaptive captured). Look at batch_form and gpu_queue spans; annotate where latency dominates.
- Next 10-60 minutes (engineer deep-dive):
  1) Correlate infra_scale_events with spike start_ts +/- 30s. If matches, look at autoscaler logs and node metrics (cpu/gpu mem, eviction).
  2) Check model_variant_fallbacks_count in that window; if non-zero, check fallback reasons (overload, version mismatch).
  3) If GPU scheduler wait is primary, inspect per-node queue lengths and kernel exec times; consider temporary capacity bump or throttling.
  4) Reproduce locally with archived request (sanitize tenant PII) via replay harness.
- Escalation and remediation:
  - If root cause is infra (autoscaler/placement): tag as ops incident, adjust scale policies or add short-term capacity; create JIRA ops task.
  - If root cause is batching behavior due to sudden fan-in on route: consider backpressure knobs (max_queue_size per route) and soft-start rate limiter for new tenants.
  - If root cause is KV cache eviction pattern: increase shard replication or tune eviction TTL for hot session tenants.

Simplicity-first alerting suggestions
- Avoid firing on single token p99 spikes. Alert when both: route-level microburst_p95 crosses threshold AND either queue_depth > X OR kv_miss_rate delta > Y. This reduces noisy pages.

Cost and retention considerations
- Full-trace capture at spike time is expensive. Limit full capture to 48h hotspot retention for post-mortem, and store lightweight trace breadcrumbs indefinitely (ids + failure tags).
- Reduce span cardinality by collapsing low-value attributes behind a feature flag (e.g., full prompt hashes) and only emit for sampled traces.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need a canonical definition for what window size qualifies as a microburst (proposal: 3–30s). Vote?
- Confirm where to store the 48h trace dump (current S3 vs ephemeral trace store). Ops input needed.
- Determine safe tenant-sampling policy to avoid leaking PII when replaying traces; add automated sanitizer hooks.
- Instrument batch_form to emit enqueue size percentiles (p50/p95) instead of only histograms — easier to trend.

Appendix: handy links and notes to self
- Confluence draft with longer theory: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Replay harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-harness (PR 12 includes sanitizer patch)
- Slack thread: #ops-microburst (recent discussion pinned)
- Short checklist to add to alert runbook: capture 3 traces, snapshot batch histogram, kv miss list, note autoscaler markers.

Notes to self (half-formed ideas):
- Could try a "microburst fingerprint" hash: combine top-3 tenant ids, predominant batch_size, and whether fallback occurred — useful to cluster repeat microbursts.
- Low-effort UI: show last offending request in banner, but redact prompt; provide a two-click replay flow.
